hint: On a number line, the greater number is always the one farther to the right. This is true for negative numbers as well.

hints.text: On a number line, the greater number is always the one farther to the right. This is true for negative numbers as well.
Place $-3$ and $-8$ on a number line. $-3$ is $3$ steps left of $0$ and $-8$ is $8$ steps left. Decide which one ends up farther right.
$-3$ is to the right of $-8$, so $-3$ is the greater number.

explanation: Greater numbers are farther right on the number line, so compare the positions of the two numbers.
$-3$ is $3$ units left of $0$ and $-8$ is $8$ units left of $0$, which puts $-3$ to the right of $-8$.
So $-3 > -8$, and the greater number is $-3$.
